title: Who Shall Inhabit in Thy Hill
description: Who Shall Inhabit in Thy Hill in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 15, part 1, headed “Characters of a saint; or, a citizen of Zion; or, The qualifications of a Christian”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Who shall in-hab-it in thy hill, O God of ho-li-ness? Whom will the Lord ad-mit to dwell So near his throne of grace?

lines: Who shall inhabit in thy hill,
O God of holiness?
Whom will the Lord admit to dwell
So near his throne of grace?
The man that walks in pious ways,
And works with righteous hands;
That trusts his Maker's promises,
And follows his commands.
He speaks the meaning of his heart,
Nor slanders with his tongue;
Will scarce believe an ill report,
Nor do his neighbour wrong.
The wealthy sinner he contemns,
Loves all that fear the Lord:
And tho' to his own hurt he swears,
Still he performs his word.
His hands disdain a golden bribe,
And never gripe the poor;
This man shall dwell with God on earth,
And find his heaven secure.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
